title: Pivot Sidebar: Contextual Routes & Smart Workspace Tabs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, adaptive left navigation (Pivot Sidebar) that surfaces context-aware routes, reduces cognitive load for multi-tenant workflows, and introduces smart workspace tabs to speed switching between dashboard/rollout/cost views. This ticket captures the research summary, low-fi and high-fi prototypes, acceptance criteria, and design-review feedback for iteration 1. Goals: (1) Make it possible to reach common console surfaces in 2 clicks from any context; (2) Surface per-workspace rollouts and cost insights without modal navigation; (3) Provide a resilient layout for future console extensions (custom routes, role-aware items).
acceptance_criteria: Pivot Sidebar collapsed state preserves primary context and reveals icons with accessible tooltips
Workspace tabs show pinned routes (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost) and persist per-workspace
Route transition preserves query/state for long-running views (logs, evaluations)
Prototype usability test median task completion <= 35s for switching between two workspaces and opening a rollout history
Design approved by PM and Eng with a high-level implementation handoff doc
decisions: We will adopt a two-tier item model: primary routes (global) and workspace lenses (per-workspace pinned routes).
Collapsed sidebar uses a dense icon-only column with hover popovers; accessibility label is mandatory for each icon.
Workspace tabs are persistent per-workspace and survive sign-out/sign-in to support multi-machine flows.
Cost and Rollout quick-previews will be implemented as lightweight slide-over panels, not full route redirects, for first iteration.
Rollups: backend will expose stable route IDs and state tokens so frontend can restore long-running queries when switching contexts.
tradeoffs: Slide-over previews avoid full navigation but add complexity for deep-linking into specific rollout steps.
Per-workspace persistence improves speed for power users but requires careful storage and migration for older workspaces.
Dense collapsed state reduces footprint but increases discovery costs for new users; mitigated via a short onboarding tooltip tour.
